about.hero_lead: An interactive platform for studying, step-by-step solving, and visualizing numerical methods and computational algorithms.
about.author_role: Karshi State University Student · Applied Mathematics
about.author_bio: This platform was developed to facilitate in-depth study of numerical analysis and computational mathematics, provide interactive solutions for laboratory assignments, and offer students an intuitive, modern STEM learning tool.
about.feat_1_desc: Real-time recalculation of formulas and graphs as input parameters change.
about.feat_2_desc: Comprehensive step-by-step audit logs demonstrating algorithm convergence.
about.feat_3_desc: High-fidelity mathematical typesetting rendered through KaTeX.
about.feat_4_desc: Single codebase powering Web, Windows/macOS desktop, and Android Tauri targets.
about.feat_5_desc: Fully localized interface in Uzbek, Russian, and English.
about.feat_6_desc: Tailored light and dark themes optimized for focus and eye comfort.
about.v1_desc: First numerical method calculators crafted using standard HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.
about.v2_desc: Expanded portal with broad method suite and theory (archived at v2.sonli-usullar.uz).
about.v3_desc: Strict TypeScript, Tailwind CSS 4, static export, and multi-target native desktop/mobile application.

dashboard.hero_lead: Learn numerical methods through real interactive computation, not just theory.
dashboard.catalog_desc: Explore all 9 core numerical computation algorithms, their mathematical formulas, and live interactive labs.
dashboard.no_methods_found: No methods found for this filter.
dashboard.desc_bisection: Find guaranteed roots of continuous equations by repeatedly bisecting intervals.
dashboard.desc_newton: Use function tangents to converge quickly to a root and inspect every iteration.
dashboard.desc_lagrange: Construct a unique polynomial interpolation passing through arbitrary data points.
dashboard.desc_rectangles: Approximate definite integrals using left, right, and midpoint rectangles.
dashboard.desc_trapezoid: Approximate curvilinear trapezoids using piecewise linear segments.
dashboard.desc_simpson: Compute definite integrals with 4th-order accuracy using parabolic interpolation.
dashboard.desc_euler: Step-by-step numerical solution of first-order initial value Cauchy problems.
dashboard.next_desc: Enter a function, interval, and precision. The system will show every step of approaching the root.
dashboard.desc_sweep: Solve tridiagonal linear systems with forward and backward sweeps.
dashboard.desc_rungeKutta: Solve a first-order initial value problem with the classical fourth-order Runge–Kutta method.

bisection.hero_lead: Guaranteed convergence to the root by halving the interval at each step.
bisection.map_1_s: Check signs of f(a) and f(b)
bisection.map_3_s: Select the subinterval with the root
bisection.note_fn: function — the equation to solve. Example:
bisection.err_fn: Check the expression to display the formula
bisection.note_eps: Precision — stop when interval length is less than this.
bisection.plot_empty: Enter a valid function and a < b for the plot
bisection.trace_empty_desc: Enter parameters on the left, then click the button.

euler.hero_lead: Compare standard and improved Euler methods with the analytical solution, observing the difference at each step.
euler.hero_condition: Designed for 1st-order Ordinary Differential Equations (ODEs) — Cauchy initial value problems.
euler.plot_exact_note: No analytical solution exists for this equation (computed numerically only).
euler.method_simple_desc: Derivative is evaluated at the current point.
euler.exact_numerical_hint: No closed-form elementary formula exists for this equation. In such cases, numerical methods like Euler's method are the only practical solution.
euler.exact_reason_nonlinear_y: The equation is non-linear with respect to y (e.g. y², √y or complex dependence). No closed-form analytical solution exists in elementary functions.
euler.exact_reason_cross: The equation contains non-separable mixed terms of x and y that cannot be integrated with elementary methods.
euler.exact_reason_general: No closed-form analytical solution in elementary functions was found for this differential equation.
euler.steps_desc: intervals, final step is adjusted to the boundary.
euler.notebook_desc: Step-by-step arithmetic solution with numerical substitutions formatted for lab notebooks.
euler.notebook_etc: ... (and so on until the final step)

newton.hero_lead: The tangent method approximates the derivative numerically and converges quadratically near a root.
newton.map_1_s: Choose a when f(a)·f''(a)>0; otherwise start from b.
newton.map_2_s: Apply xₙ₊₁ = xₙ − f(xₙ)/f′(xₙ) using a numerical derivative.
newton.note_method: The tangent to the function graph meets the x-axis at the next root estimate.
newton.note_start: Following V2, choose a when f(a)·f''(a)>0; otherwise use endpoint b.
newton.note_derivative: As in V2, f′(x) ≈ [f(x+h)−f(x)]/h, with h=10⁻⁶.
newton.exact_endpoint: f({endpoint}) = 0, so the root is exactly at that endpoint.
newton.step_done_desc: The step difference is below ε, so the root estimate has converged.
newton.step_continue_desc: The step difference is not yet below ε; continue from xₙ₊₁.
newton.trace_empty_desc: Enter a function or choose an example, then calculate to inspect every tangent iteration.
newton.exact_title: An exact root was found at an endpoint

simpson.hero_lead: Parabolic rule. Numerically evaluate definite integrals using quadratic interpolation with high precision.
simpson.hero_condSub: The number of subintervals 'n' must be an even integer
simpson.map_1_s: Interval is divided into n equal parts: h = (b - a) / n.
simpson.map_1_desc: Interval is divided into n equal parts:
simpson.map_2_s: Endpoints, odd, and even index function values are separated.
simpson.note_fn: Integrand expression (e.g. dx / sqrt(1 + 2x^2), sin(x), x^2).
simpson.plot_empty: Enter valid bounds and expression to plot the curve and integral area.

trapezoid.hero_lead: Approximate the integrand linearly between nodes and calculate every trapezoid area step by step.
trapezoid.hero_condition: The integrand is approximated linearly on each subinterval.
trapezoid.map_2_desc: Calculate xᵢ and f(xᵢ) for each node
trapezoid.note_fn: Use Math.js syntax. Expressions containing dx are also accepted:
trapezoid.plot_empty: Enter a function and bounds with a < b to plot.
trapezoid.step_nodes_desc: Each node is found with xᵢ = a + i·h, then f(xᵢ) is evaluated.
trapezoid.benchmark_note: The benchmark is not an analytical exact integral: as in the V2 version, it is a higher-resolution approximation computed by the trapezoidal rule with n = {count} subintervals.
trapezoid.empty_desc: Enter the parameters on the left. The result will show nodes, each trapezoid area, their sum, and the comparison steps.
trapezoid.footer: Trapezoidal rule · Piecewise linear interpolation over n equal subintervals

rectangle.hero_lead: Calculate areas from endpoint function values, then compare the left, right, averaged rectangle sums, and trapezoidal estimate.
rectangle.hero_condition: Average the left and right sums for a balanced approximation.
rectangle.note_fn: Use Math.js syntax. Expressions containing dx are also accepted:
rectangle.plot_empty: Enter a function and bounds with a < b to plot.
rectangle.step_nodes_desc: Find each node using xᵢ = a + i·h and evaluate f(xᵢ).
rectangle.benchmark_note: The benchmark is not an analytical exact integral: as in V2, it is a higher-resolution approximation using the trapezoidal rule with n = {count} subintervals.
rectangle.error_note: Errors are measured against the higher-resolution benchmark. This benchmark is not an analytical exact value.
rectangle.empty_desc: Enter the parameters. The result will show left, right, and averaged sums, every rectangle step, and a comparison.
rectangle.footer: Left/right rectangles · Mean value · Trapezoid comparison

lagrange.hero_lead: Build basis polynomials from your data points, combine them into one interpolating polynomial, then inspect its value at any x.
lagrange.hero_condition: The unique polynomial through distinct x nodes.
lagrange.map_1_desc: Provide a yᵢ value for every xᵢ
lagrange.note_points: x and y values may be numbers or fractions, for example:
lagrange.note_end: . Each x value must be distinct.
lagrange.point_controls: Add a point or remove the last one
lagrange.step_sum_desc: Multiply each yᵢ value by its ℓᵢ(x) basis polynomial and sum the terms.
lagrange.error_substitution: Since f(x) was provided, the practical difference at this point is:
lagrange.remainder_note: Here ξ is an unknown point between the nodes and x*. Without the derivative values of f, the theoretical remainder cannot be evaluated numerically.
lagrange.empty_desc: Enter nodes or choose an example. Calculate to reveal the basis polynomials, final polynomial, its value, and the optional error check.
lagrange.footer: Lagrange formula · Distinct x nodes · Polynomial degree at most n

errors.nwt_params: Require a < b and precision ε > 0.
errors.nwt_fn: The function is undefined at an evaluation point or its numerical derivative could not be computed.
errors.nwt_deriv_zero: Error: derivative became zero (f'(x) ≈ 0) at step {iter}.
errors.nwt_no_root: Root not found within {max} iterations. The method may not converge from this starting point.
errors.bis_undef: Function is undefined at the given points.
errors.bis_same_sign: Signs of f(a) and f(b) are the same: f(a)={fa}, f(b)={fb}. Root bracketing requires f(a)·f(b) < 0.
errors.bis_done: Interval length is less than ε — calculation stopped.
errors.bis_left: Signs of f(a) and f(c) are opposite. Root is in the left half.
errors.bis_right: Signs of f(c) and f(b) are opposite. Root is in the right half.
errors.bis_dec_left: Since f(a) · f(c) < 0, new interval [a, c] = {interval}
errors.bis_dec_right: Since f(c) · f(b) < 0, new interval [c, b] = {interval}

errors.elr_bounds: x_end must be greater than x₀, and step h must be > 0.
errors.elr_max: The number of steps must not exceed 1000.
errors.elr_syntax: Check function syntax. Use Math.js syntax.
errors.elr_finite: f({x}, {y}) is not a finite number.
errors.smp_params: Invalid parameters. Please check your numerical inputs.
errors.smp_bounds: Lower bound (a) must be strictly less than upper bound (b) (a < b).
errors.smp_positive: Subintervals count (n) must be a positive integer.
errors.smp_eval: Could not evaluate f({x}) or function evaluated to infinity/NaN.
errors.trap_params: Enter numeric values for a, b, and n; n must be an integer.
errors.trap_bounds: The lower bound a must be less than the upper bound b.
errors.trap_positive: The number of subintervals n must be at least 1.
errors.trap_max: The number of subintervals must not exceed {max}.
errors.trap_fn: Check the function expression and use Math.js syntax.
errors.trap_eval: Could not evaluate f({x}); the function must be defined on the interval.
errors.rect_params: Enter numeric values for a, b, and n; n must be an integer.
errors.rect_bounds: The lower bound a must be less than the upper bound b.
errors.rect_positive: The number of subintervals n must be at least 1.
errors.rect_max: The number of subintervals must not exceed {max}.
errors.rect_fn: Check the function expression and use Math.js syntax.
errors.rect_eval: Could not evaluate f({x}); the function must be defined on the whole interval.
errors.lag_points_min: Lagrange interpolation requires at least 2 points.
errors.lag_points_max: The number of points must not exceed {max}.
errors.lag_point_value: Check the x and y values for point {point}.
errors.lag_duplicate: All x nodes must be distinct.
errors.lag_x: Enter the evaluation x* as a number or fraction.
errors.lag_target: Check the optional f(x) expression and use Math.js syntax.
errors.sweep_rows: System size must be between {min} and {max}.
errors.sweep_number: Every value in row {row} must be numeric.

syntax.hero_lead: For the program to work correctly, all expressions (formulas) must be written in strict accordance with Math.js syntax.

sweep.hero_lead: Solve tridiagonal linear systems with the Thomas algorithm and inspect every intermediate coefficient.
sweep.hero_condition: a₁ = 0 and cₙ = 0; pivots must remain non-zero.
sweep.map_1_s: Compute αᵢ and βᵢ coefficients row by row.
sweep.map_2_s: Recover xᵢ values from xₙ back to x₁.
sweep.map_3_s: Evaluate rᵢ = dᵢ − (aᵢxᵢ₋₁+bᵢxᵢ+cᵢxᵢ₊₁) for every row.
sweep.goal_text: Solving tridiagonal systems of linear equations.
sweep.residual_formula_note: Due to value rounding, residuals should be very close to zero.
sweep.note_method: An O(n) solver for systems whose non-zero entries lie on the main and two neighboring diagonals.
sweep.note_precision: Formulas use the selected display precision; residuals are evaluated using full internal precision.
sweep.matrix_hint: Boundary entries a₁ and cₙ are fixed at 0 automatically.
sweep.check_note: The closer each residual is to zero, the more accurately the solution satisfies the system.
sweep.empty_desc: Review the matrix coefficients and start the calculation.

rk4.title: Runge–Kutta
rk4.lead: Advance a first-order initial value problem with four slope estimates per step, then inspect the full calculation table and solution curve.
rk4.chart_note: Compare the RK4 approximation with the exact solution of this example.
rk4.no_chart: Enter valid parameters to display the chart.
rk4.expression_hint: Math.js syntax; for example: x^2 + y, x-y, or sin(x)+y.
rk4.exact_unavailable: An exact solution could not be derived for this expression. The RK4 numerical result is still available.
rk4.chart_note_no_exact: Only the RK4 numerical approximation is shown because no exact solution was derived.
rk4.exact_description: Symbolically derived from the entered first-order differential equation and initial condition.
